explanation.text: The key missing meat-like notes in pea protein versus a cooked beef burger are sulfur-containing compounds such as 2-methyl-3-furanthiol and 2-furfurylthiol (meaty, roasted descriptors) [1-s2.0-S0963996926007192-main.pdf p.9.0], Maillard reaction products including pyrazines [foods-12-00923.pdf p.4.0], and free glutamic acid contributing umami character [1-s2.0-S0924224421002764-main.pdf p.11.0]. Pea protein's dominant off-notes are hexanal and heptanal (beany, green, grassy) [foods-13-03423.pdf p.1.0] [foods-14-03363.pdf p.18.0], alkyl methoxypyrazines such as 2-isobutyl-3-methoxypyrazine (green, earthy) [s11947-025-03898-3.pdf p.2.0] [Plant_protein_flavor_chemistry_fundamentals_and_te.pdf p.4.0], 1-octen-3-ol and 2-pentylfuran (beany, earthy) [foods-15-00039.pdf p.13.0], and bitter/astringent saponins and polyphenols [cosson2022.pdf p.1.0]. The top-ranked levers are a D-xylose and L-cysteine Maillard reaction system to generate 2-methyl-3-furanthiol and 2-furfurylthiol [1-s2.0-S0963996926007192-main.pdf p.1.0], sequential lactic acid bacteria fermentation to reduce hexanal, 2-pentylfuran, 1-octen-3-ol, and methoxypyrazines [foods-15-00039.pdf p.9.0], and beta-cyclodextrin to encapsulate residual beany off-flavors [journal.pone.0269278.pdf p.8.0].
